With access to a diverse co-curricular programme, students are accomplished all-rounders with university statements studded with personal achievements and successes. Our students leave us in Year 13 with determination and clearly defined ambition, ready to make their mark on the world.
The Pioneer cohort of girls and boys in Years 7 and 12 begin a new chapter in our 300‑year story. Together, they benefit from the exceptional academic and pastoral experience that defines our school.

Careers & Higher Education
Students are supported by a comprehensive careers programme, including annual careers and Higher Education fairs, providing students with accurate and impartial careers advice.
Students enjoy a comprehensive careers programme including access to Higher Educational Fairs to provide accurate and impartial careers advice. Our Careers department is here to advise and support students and their parents in making choices that are right for them throughout their school career. This includes giving students clear guidance on the options available to them and the wider implications around those choices. Guidance provided will help students make informed GCSE and A Level decisions, giving them the very best chance of fulfilling their potential.
Throughout their time at SWPS, students develop their skills in many ways – not only in their academic studies but also in holding positions of responsibility, leading teams, making presentations and participating in a wide variety of co-curricular activities. These develop many of the transferable skills essential for the world of work.
Our Careers department enables students to identify their strengths, weaknesses and interests relating to the world of work. By learning about different careers and opportunities, they will be able to identify the best options for them individually through one to one support and guidance.
Lucy Haley, Head of Careers

pageCache.pageTitle: Personalised Learning | Sir William Perkins's School (SWPS)
pageCache.text:
Personalised Learning
At SWPS we believe our fundamental purpose is to challenge all our students intellectually and inspire them to be successful learners whatever challenges they face.
We prepare our students for a life of learning and self-understanding. Confidence and flexibility in their approach to learning means our students can adapt to whatever the future holds for them.
The school recognises that high quality teaching, adapted for individual students, is the first step to responding to students who have or may have SEND, such as Dyslexia, Attention Deficit or neurodiversity.
The Personalised Learning Department caters for students with mild special educational needs and disabilities, and our qualified and experienced specialist teachers provide a range of provisions for our students.
Class teachers are the first people to offer support to the student in order for their potential to be achieved. Students’ needs are reviewed regularly, and individual support may be offered outside of lessons to augment the support given in class.
Further information about the support available for students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), including those with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), and for students with English as an Additional Language (EAL), can be found in our Students with SEND Policy and Students with EAL Policy, available elsewhere on our website.
Whole School Approach
Integral to our success with students is close liaison with parents, tutors, subject staff, the pastoral team and other agencies.
Support at SWPS is a whole school approach which is reinforced by the expertise of the Personalised Learning Department. For those students who need further specialist support and tuition, tailored lessons are provided to help the student flourish and achieve, in spite of the challenges they may face.
Teachers know their pupils well and manage their lessons with specific needs or sensitivities of individuals in mind.
Exams & Access Arrangements
The Head of Personalised Learning manages all access arrangements for internal and external examinations and works closely with the Exams Officer to ensure all access arrangements follow the JCQ and CAIE guidelines. If a student receives an exam concession, then we may ask that an updated report is completed by our centre-approved Educational Psychologist in Year 9.

Community & Partnerships
Partnerships at SWPS
Partnership is one of the defining pillars of our strategic vision at Sir William Perkins’s School. We are committed to building purposeful, high-impact relationships that extend learning beyond the classroom, open doors for our students, and contribute meaningfully to our wider community.
Over the past year, we have significantly strengthened and expanded our partnerships across education, sport, industry and the local community. These collaborations are not simply additive – they are transformational. They enrich the student experience, enhance teaching and learning, and ensure that every SWPS student is connected, confident and world ready.
Training the Teachers of Tomorrow
As part of our commitment to educational excellence, SWPS plays an active role in shaping the next generation of teachers.
We are proud to partner with leading Initial Teacher Training providers, including St Mary’s University, Twickenham, an Ofsted Outstanding centre, and our newest partner, i2i Teaching Partnership.
Through these collaborations, we provide a dynamic and supportive training environment where trainee teachers can thrive. From September, we are delighted to welcome trainees in Computer Science and Physics,further strengthening our academic community.
Our approach is hands-on, immersive and aspirational. Trainees benefit from expert mentoring, diverse classroom experience, and the opportunity to contribute to a vibrant school environment. Increasingly, we are also seeing former SWPS students return to the profession – and to our classrooms – a powerful reflection of the impact of our community.
Sporting Excellence Through Collaboration
Sport at SWPS is powered by partnership. By working with leading clubs, coaches and organisations, we provide our students with exceptional access to expertise, facilities and pathways beyond school.
Our programme includes collaborations with organisations such as Reading FC Community Trust, Guildford Hockey Club, Spelthorne Tennis Centre and Runnymede Raptors Basketball Club, alongside a wide network of local clubs and performance providers.
These partnerships enable us to:
At the same time, our facilities and programmes support the wider sporting community, reinforcing our role as a hub for sport in the local area.

These experiences are mutually beneficial – supporting partner schools while developing leadership, communication and confidence in our own students.
Real-World Learning Through Industry Partnerships
Our partnerships with businesses and higher education institutions bring learning to life and prepare students for a rapidly evolving world.
Through initiatives such as our Industry Challenge Programme, students have worked directly with organisations including Tesco, IGF and HCL Technologies, tackling real-world challenges and presenting solutions in professional settings.
We have also collaborated with universities and national organisations to deliver specialist academic experiences, including advanced STEM workshops.
These opportunities empower students to think critically, work collaboratively and engage with the world beyond school with ambition and purpose.
Community Impact
Partnership at SWPS goes beyond education – it is about making a positive difference.
Our students are actively involved in community initiatives, including volunteering programmes and collaborative projects with local schools, charities and organisations across Runnymede. Flagship events such as Make a Difference Day see our students working directly within the community, developing empathy, leadership and a strong sense of social responsibility.
We are also continuing to grow our involvement in wider initiatives, including collaborative education projects and community-focused programmes that strengthen local connections and create lasting impact.

pageCache.pageTitle: Record A Level results and Oxbridge success for Sir William Perkins's Students with 91% of grades A*- B | Sir William Perkins's School (SWPS)
pageCache.text:
Record A Level results and Oxbridge success for Sir William Perkins’s Students with 91% of grades A*- B
Record A Level results and Oxbridge success for Sir William Perkins’s Students with 91% of grades A*- B
Students at Sir William Perkins’s School in Chertsey are celebrating a year of exceptional examination success, with outstanding A Level results accompanied by record success in applications to Oxford and Cambridge and progression to an impressive range of high-tariff universities. Nearly 40% of our students achieved a clean sweep of A*-A grades.
Alongside exceptional academic outcomes, this year’s leavers have secured places on some of the country’s most competitive degree programmes. From Medicine, Physiotherapy, PPE, Psychology, Interior Design, Neuroscience, Linguistics and English Language and Literature, SWPS students will embark on a breadth of pathways that reflects the richness of their interests and ambitions.
Debbie Picton, Head, said: “These results represent far more than a set of grades. They reflect years of intellectual curiosity, ambition, resilience and personal growth. We are incredibly proud of our students and all they have achieved, both inside and beyond the classroom.
“This year has brought record Oxbridge success and outstanding destinations across a huge range of disciplines, but what is most pleasing is seeing each student move forward to a pathway that genuinely excites and inspires them. Every individual’s journey looks different, and that is something we celebrate at Sir William Perkins’s.”
Excellence is both diverse and consistent at SWPS because of the strength of the school’s broad and ambitious Sixth Form curriculum allowing them to follow bespoke pathways. Students have excelled across Maths with 65% of candidates achieving A* – A and 100% achieving A-B. English students also shone with 85% of the grades at the top A* – A and 100% of our Art, Computer Science, DT, Further Maths, Geography, German and Music candidates all achieved A* – A grades. This demonstrates that academic excellence flourishes in many different forms. The diversity of university destinations and courses reflects a community in which students are encouraged to pursue their interests with confidence and purpose.
At SWPS, examination success is matched by the remarkable achievements students enjoy beyond the classroom. Throughout their time in the Sixth Form, members of the Class of 2026 have distinguished themselves through leadership, sporting success, creative accomplishment, community engagement, entrepreneurship and academic enrichment. Recent highlights include achievements in rowing, dramatic performance, music, sustainability initiatives, public speaking, academic competitions, charitable projects and student-led research endeavours, reflecting a cohort that has embraced opportunity in all its forms.
The Extended Project Qualification continues to play a significant role in enriching students’ academic experience, allowing them to investigate subjects of personal passion in depth. Projects undertaken this year have spanned a wide range of disciplines, from topics such as US sanctions on Cuba, China’s One-Child Policy, research into fasting and cognitive function, dietary interventions and autism, cosmetic product safety and questions around criminal responsibility, preparing students exceptionally well for university study and future careers. 89% of students achieved A* – B grades for their projects.
Mat Dodd, Director of Sixth Form, commented: “What makes these results particularly special is that they tell the story of individual students who have been encouraged to discover who they are and what they want to contribute to the world. Our students leave SWPS with excellent qualifications, but also with the confidence, independence and sense of purpose that will help them thrive long after their time here has ended.
“Whether progressing to Medicine, Interior Design, Neuroscience, Linguistics or countless other fields, they have embraced opportunities both within and beyond the curriculum and should be immensely proud of what they have accomplished.”
These achievements are a powerful reflection of the school’s commitment to ensuring that every student is known, valued and supported as an individual. Through small class sizes, expert teaching, outstanding pastoral care and an extensive co-curricular programme, students are empowered to develop their talents, explore new interests and fulfil their potential. This commitment to championing the individual remains at the heart of the school’s success. By combining academic rigour with rich opportunities beyond the classroom, SWPS prepares students not simply for further study, but for life. Our leavers depart as confident, compassionate and intellectually curious young people, ready to embrace opportunity and make a meaningful contribution in an interconnected world.
As SWPS celebrates another year of exceptional outcomes, the school is also entering an exciting new chapter in its 300-year history. This September, the School will welcome its first co-educational Year 7 and Year 12 cohorts, marking the beginning of a phased transition to becoming fully co-educational by 2030. The move reflects the school’s belief in preparing young people for the world beyond school, creating an educational environment that more closely mirrors the diverse society in which students will live, study and work. Built on a longstanding reputation for academic excellence, outstanding pastoral care and a culture where every young person is encouraged to flourish, SWPS looks forward to extending these opportunities to a new generation of students.
“The future of SWPS is incredibly exciting,” added Ms Picton. “As we welcome the first boys into Years 7 and 12 this September, we remain absolutely committed to the qualities that have defined the school for generations: exceptional teaching, ambitious opportunities and a genuine understanding of every individual student. Today’s results demonstrate what is possible when young people are challenged, supported and inspired to achieve their very best.”

SWPS Sixth Form Students Inspire Young Language Learners at Staines Prep
Our Sixth Form students recently visited Staines Prep School to deliver a fun and engaging Spanish lesson as part of our growing partnerships programme.
The session was packed with energy as the younger pupils learnt new Spanish vocabulary through games, activities and the much-loved Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes song. Singing together helped build confidence while introducing children to a new language in an enjoyable and memorable way.
For our Sixth Form students, the visit provided a valuable opportunity to develop their leadership, communication and teaching skills. Planning and delivering lessons to younger pupils encouraged them to think creatively, adapt their approach and build confidence in leading others – skills that will benefit them well beyond school.
The visit also reflects SWPS’s commitment to working in partnership with our local community, creating meaningful opportunities for students to make a positive impact while inspiring a love of learning in younger children.
We are incredibly proud of our Sixth Form students for representing the school so enthusiastically and look forward to continuing our partnership with Staines Prep through future collaborative activities.

Holiday Training
Due to the physiologically demanding nature of the sport, structured rowing training continues during holiday periods (other than the summer break). Training provision will be set at an appropriate level for each age-group to continue the rowers’ development throughout the season.
Training Camps
At Perkins we hold two annual training camps.
The first is in October Half-Term for our Senior Squad (Year 11-13), and is a non-residential camp on the river in Pangbourne, giving our rowers the chance to row on a beautiful, longer stretch of the Thames, perfect for long distance work.
The second is for Year 10-13 rowers, during the Easter holidays at an overseas warm weather venue. This camp is used to help develop our athletes and racing crews ahead of the summer regatta season, with the prestigious National Schools’ Regatta just six weeks away.

The Governors of Sir William Perkins’s School are committed to broadening access to the school by offering means-tested financial assistance with the payment of school fees through the Perkins Foundation. A limited number of means-tested financial awards are available to families of students joining Year 7 or Year 12 and are worth, in some cases, up to 100% of tuition fees.
Bursary awards are subject to an annual review and may be varied upwards or downwards, depending on any changes to parental circumstances.

Scholarships
Sir William Perkins’s School has much to offer individuals who demonstrate outstanding talent and potential in their chosen fields. Scholarships are designed to recognise and develop pupils’ talents, interests and aptitudes, whilst providing them with both enrichment and support.
SWPS offers a range of scholarships to pupils entering the school at Year 7, Year 9 and Year 12 including Academic, Art and Design, Drama, Music, Sport and STEM, and are worth up to 10% of the current tuition fees. The number and value of scholarships awards vary from year to year and awards are at the discretion of the Head. All scholarships, which can be held for the whole of a pupil’s time at SWPS subject to the terms and conditions of each award, are reviewed annually. We look forward to award-holders remaining at SWPS until they have completed their A Level examinations, thus making a significant contribution to school life.
Aspire Programme
Strong candidates who are not awarded a full Academic, Music, Art, Drama, Sport or STEM Scholarship may be invited to join our ‘Aspire’ programme. This gives students the opportunity to join Scholarship activities and take up opportunities such as peer mentoring and specialist trips in recognition of their ability and commitment to their chosen field. Whilst there is no fee remission for being on the Aspire programme, it is nevertheless a prestigious opportunity and one which will allow the students to develop their specialist interest and talent extensively.
Rewards & Responsibility
Receiving an award carries a level of prestige but also a degree of expectation. Scholars will be expected to act as role models in their fields of interest, and – as they move into their senior years – to begin to deliver on their potential by taking on positions of leadership.
We have developed a programme of extension activities and opportunities appropriate to particular areas of talent; Music and Drama scholars, for example, attend regular masterclasses with visiting professionals, as well as perform in scholars’ recitals and school productions.

Throughout our history, our scholars have enriched the life of the School with their energy, creativity, and leadership. And beyond our walls, they’ve gone on to make their mark on the world, carrying the spirit of SWPS with them.
If you’re ready to challenge yourself, grow your talents, and be part of a vibrant, supportive community, a scholarship at SWPS could be your next step.

Sixth Form Registration
SWPS Sixth Form offers far more than outstanding A Level results alone.
Our distinctive ‘3 A Levels +’ and Futures Programme approach combines academic excellence with leadership opportunities, personalised career guidance, enrichment and exceptional pastoral support, preparing students for university, careers and life beyond school.
Students join our co-educational Sixth Form from a wide range of local schools and quickly become part of our welcoming and ambitious community.
Please contact our Admissions Team at Admissions@swps.org.uk for late applications for September 2026 or in-year registrations.
“SWPS gives students the confidence to lead, contribute ideas and make the most of every opportunity.”
Admissions process
1. Apply online
2. Interviews
3. Scholarships
4. Decision
1. Apply online
Registration for entry to Year 12 in September 2027 is now open, with a deadline of noon on Thursday 15 October to apply. We encourage families to register early due to strong interest in SWPS Sixth Form.
2. Interviews
All applicants will be invited to interview with the Head and Director of Sixth Form, and meet with the Heads of Department of the subjects they wish to study at A Level. We will also request a report from your current school notifying us of your predicted grades for GCSE.
3. Scholarships
Scholarships are available for students demonstrating exceptional talent in Academic study, Art, Drama, Music, Rowing and Sport, with assessments taking place in late November.
4. Decision
Decisions will be emailed to parents in December 2026 and offers are conditional upon students achieving at least six GCSE grades at Grade 7. The deadline for acceptance will be Wednesday 16 December 2026 at noon.

Year 7 Registration
Joining SWPS at Year 7 is the beginning of an exciting seven-year journey. Families choose SWPS for its balance of academic ambition, exceptional pastoral care and the confidence students develop both inside and outside the classroom.
From September 2026, SWPS will welcome both boys and girls into Year 7 as part of our move to full co-education. Interest in Year 7 2026 entry has already been exceptionally high, as families look to become part of this pioneering new chapter in the school’s 300-year history. Early registration is strongly encouraged.
Please contact our Admissions Team at Admissions@swps.org.uk if you would like to make a late application or in-year registration.
“SWPS is a nurturing and inclusive community where students are encouraged to grow in confidence and embrace every opportunity.”
Admissions process
1. Apply online
2. Assessments and Interview
3. Scholarships
4. Decision
1. Apply online
Registration for entry in September 2027 and deferred entry in September 2029 is now open, with a deadline of noon on Thursday 15 October 2026 to apply.
2. Assessments and Interview
All applicants will be invited to sit the entrance test at Sir William Perkins’s School on Saturday 14 November 2026. They will sit Maths and English assessments and meet with a senior member of staff as part of the admissions process. These conversations are designed to help us get to know each student, their interests and aspirations. Sample papers are provided below to help students feel familiar and confident ahead of the assessment day.

3. Scholarships
Scholarships are available for students demonstrating exceptional potential in Academic study, Art, Drama, Music, Sport and STEM, with assessments and auditions taking place in late November.

Decisions will be emailed to parents in December 2026. The deadline for acceptance will be March 2027, when a deposit will be required to secure your place.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 9 Registration | Sir William Perkins's School (SWPS)
pageCache.text:
Year 9 Registration
Joining SWPS at Year 9 offers students a dynamic and purposeful start to their senior school journey, at a crucial point just ahead of GCSE study. They become part of a warm, ambitious and high-achieving community where confidence grows quickly, friendships flourish, and strong academic foundations are firmly established. Exceptional pastoral care sits at the heart of this experience, alongside a rich and varied co-curricular programme that encourages every student to explore, contribute and thrive.
As SWPS moves towards full co-education, Year 9 remains a vibrant and well-established entry point, offering both continuity and exciting new opportunities within an evolving school community.
Families choosing Year 9 entry value the space it provides for students to settle, grow and feel fully at home in senior school life before GCSEs begin. With small class sizes, personalised support and a strong sense of belonging, students are empowered to aim high and approach the next stage of their education with confidence and ambition.
"Joining SWPS in Year 9, I quickly formed strong friendships and a real sense of belonging."
Admissions process
1. Apply online
2. Assessments and Interview
3. Scholarships
4. Decision
1. Apply online
Registration for 13+ entry in September 2027 and 13+ deferred entry in September 2029 is now open, with a deadline of noon on Thursday 15 October to apply. We encourage families to register early due to strong interest in Year 9 entry.
2. Assessments and Interview
All applicants will be invited to sit the entrance test at Sir William Perkins’s School on Saturday 14 November 2026. Students will take Maths and English papers and will each have an interview with a senior member of staff.
Please contact our Admissions Team at admissions@swps.org.uk if you would like to make a late application or in-year registration.
3. Scholarships
Academic, Art, Drama, Music, Sport and STEM Scholarships are offered and assessments and auditions will take place in late November.
4. Decision
Decisions will be emailed to parents in December 2026. The deadline for acceptance will be March 2027, when a deposit will be required to secure your place. Students accepting a deferred entry place will be required to submit a deferred payment deposit at this time as well.

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE Results | Sir William Perkins's School (SWPS)
pageCache.text:
GCSE Results
Sir William Perkins’s School prides itself not only on excellent academic outcomes but also on the achievements students make and the experiences they have outside of the classroom.
GCSE Results 2026
Students at Sir William Perkins’s School in Chertsey are celebrating another year of excellent GCSE results, with outcomes that reflect the School’s longstanding commitment to championing the individual. Results have remained consistently strong in recent years, with more than 80% of grades awarded at 9-7 on average.
While the headline figures are impressive, the real story behind today’s success is the School’s ability to bring out the very best in every student. Through adaptive teaching, outstanding pastoral care and a culture in which every young person is known, valued and supported as an individual, SWPS continues to achieve excellent outcomes across a broad range of abilities, interests and aspirations, perfectly positioning the School for co-education.
Debbie Picton, Head, commented: “We are incredibly proud of our students and all they have achieved. These outcomes are the result of hard work, determination and a genuine commitment to learning from our students, supported by teachers and staff who go above and beyond every day to help them succeed.”
“At SWPS, we recognise that every student’s journey is different. By understanding the strengths, ambitions and needs of each individual, we are able to provide the challenge, encouragement and support that enables young people to flourish. The consistently strong results we see year after year are a reflection of that personalised approach.”
The results reflect the success of a broad and ambitious curriculum in which students excel across STEM subjects, Languages, the Arts and Humanities alike. Particularly strong outcomes were achieved in a number of key subjects. In Mathematics and Further Mathematics, 88% of grades were awarded at 9-7, while 93% of grades achieved in English Language and English Literature were at 9-7. Modern Languages also performed exceptionally well, with 92% of students achieving grades 9-7 in French, our most popular language at GCSE. Across Biology, Chemistry and Physics, more than half of all grades (52%) were awarded at grades 9-8, underlining the strength of scientific study at the School.
This breadth of achievement, spanning quantitative disciplines, languages, humanities and the creative subjects, demonstrates the School’s belief that excellence takes many forms and that young people thrive when they are encouraged to pursue their individual talents and passions.
Today’s results are the culmination of a journey that, for many students, began when they joined SWPS in Year 7. Through a carefully structured programme of academic challenge, enrichment opportunities and pastoral support, students develop the confidence, resilience and intellectual curiosity that underpin success at GCSE and beyond. The foundations established in the early years of Senior School provide the building blocks for future success in Sixth Form, university and life beyond education.
Alongside strong academic performance, members of the Year 11 cohort have distinguished themselves through a wealth of co-curricular achievements. Students have embraced opportunities in rowing, sport, music, drama, leadership, sustainability projects, charitable initiatives and academic enrichment. These experiences develop the confidence, adaptability and character that help students succeed not only in examinations but as individuals ready to make a positive contribution to the wider world.
Peter Forrest-Biggs, Deputy Head Academic, said: “What is particularly pleasing is seeing students achieve success across such a broad range of disciplines and interests. From outstanding outcomes in English and French to exceptional performances in Mathematics, Further Mathematics and the Sciences, these results demonstrate that academic excellence is thriving across the curriculum. They are evidence of an educational approach that values the individual and ensures every student is supported to achieve their personal best.”
For those Year 11 students who continue their journey at SWPS Sixth Form, they will benefit from a highly personalised programme of study, enrichment and university preparation. The School also looks forward to welcoming Mr Harris Clough as Director of Sixth Form in September. Bringing significant experience and a clear vision for the future, he will build on the Sixth Form’s strong record of university destinations and academic success, ensuring that students continue to thrive both academically and personally.
As SWPS celebrates another year of excellent outcomes, the School is also entering an exciting new chapter in its 300-year history. This September, Sir William Perkins’s School will welcome its first co-educational Year 7 and Year 12 cohorts, beginning a phased transition to becoming fully co-educational by 2030.
The move reflects the School’s commitment to preparing young people for life in a diverse, interconnected and rapidly changing world while remaining true to the values that have shaped generations of students.
“Our mission has always been to champion the individual and help every young person become the very best version of themselves,” added Ms Picton. “As we welcome the first boys into Years 7 and 12 this September, we remain committed to the qualities that define an SWPS education: academic excellence, outstanding pastoral care and a genuine understanding of every student’s unique strengths and aspirations.”
